SCALABILITY.TITLE: Future scalability
SCALABILITY.PARAGRAPH: We build flexible, adaptable software so your company can evolve without limitations, ensuring sustainable and efficient growth.

FAQ.TITLE: FAQ
FAQ.Q1: How do you ensure the software can scale in the future?
FAQ.A1: We design from the start with a flexible structure that allows modifications and growth without compromising performance. The software architecture is organized into independent modules, making it easier to add new features and optimize existing ones without affecting the entire system. We also perform load testing to measure behavior under different demand levels.
FAQ.Q2: What security measures do you implement in applications?
FAQ.A2: Software is developed following security best practices to minimize vulnerabilities. We apply access controls, data encryption, and authentication protocols that protect information integrity. We also conduct periodic reviews to identify potential risks and keep systems protected against new threats.
FAQ.Q3: Do you provide support and maintenance after development?
FAQ.A3: Yes, maintenance is part of the process to ensure the software continues to work correctly over time. This includes fixing possible errors, optimizing processes, and updating dependencies when necessary. We also monitor systems to detect and resolve incidents proactively.
FAQ.Q4: How do you make sure the software is easy to use?
FAQ.A4: Before development begins, we analyze processes and end-user needs to define an intuitive structure. Functional prototypes are created to evaluate usability before implementation. During development, we test with users to detect difficulties and make adjustments that improve the user experience without compromising functionality.
FAQ.Q5: How do you verify the software works properly before delivery?
FAQ.A5: Before delivery, the software goes through multiple testing phases. Automated and manual tests are performed to detect errors, evaluate performance, and ensure all functionalities behave as expected. We also test in pre-production environments, where the software runs under conditions similar to real use, ensuring a stable implementation.
FAQ.Q6: How do you manage timelines and project delivery?
FAQ.A6: Each project is planned in stages with defined objectives and estimated development times. Before starting, we establish a work schedule with specific milestones to track progress and make adjustments if needed. Communication with the client is constant, allowing us to address issues without affecting agreed timelines.

SHOWCASE.LABEL: Results
SHOWCASE.TITLE: Systems we build from scratch to solve real operations
SHOWCASE.SUBTITLE: Each one started from a concrete problem, not from an idea.

ITEM1.TITLE: Quotes, follow-up, and sales lived in WhatsApp and spreadsheets
ITEM1.BEFORE: Three sales reps spent 20 minutes per quote. Customer data was scattered across chats, files, and calendars. There was no database and no formal follow-up.
ITEM1.AFTER: The CRM integrates WhatsApp Business. AI reads the conversation and pre-fills the quote while the rep is still chatting. It validates data, generates the PDF, and sends it from the same system. Follow-up, scheduling, and reporting update automatically.

ITEM2.TITLE: 3 stores and one warehouse with no inventory visibility or sales control
ITEM2.BEFORE: There was no way to know what inventory existed per location without asking. Quotes were handled separately and, once approved, sales had to be entered manually.
ITEM2.AFTER: An ERP centralizes inventory by location and converts quotes into sales without duplicating data. It includes role-based access, AI-powered reports, and direct integration with e-commerce and invoicing.

ITEM3.TITLE: Field technicians without records, per-visit billing, and scheduling in manual calendars
ITEM3.BEFORE: More than seven technicians were coordinated manually. There was no subscription model. Visits were billed one by one and there was no evidence of what happened in each service.
ITEM3.AFTER: The system schedules visits by subscription frequency and flags pending payments. Technicians log each service with photos, customer signature, and geolocation from mobile. Management approves reports before sending them to the client.

ITEM4.TITLE: All appointments went through call center, WhatsApp, or front desk
ITEM4.BEFORE: The clinic's internal system worked well, but patients could not self-manage anything. Every appointment required human assistance.
ITEM4.AFTER: A web scheduler was connected to the existing internal system. Patients book using real-time availability, without replacing what already worked and without duplicating data.

ITEM5.TITLE: Ticket sales depended on a third party charging commission per ticket
ITEM5.BEFORE: Creating an event required notifying the provider via WhatsApp. Access was validated with downloaded lists and commissions were paid per sold ticket.
ITEM5.AFTER: A first-party ticketing system integrated into the website was implemented. Online purchase, automatic QR by email, scan app at the gate, and refunds from a management panel. No middlemen and no commissions.

ITEM6.TITLE: 5 customer types with different conditions and all sales depended on reps
ITEM6.BEFORE: There was no online sales channel. Every order required a sales rep to apply prices and business rules manually based on customer type inside the ERP.
ITEM6.AFTER: The e-commerce platform recognizes customer types and automatically applies commercial conditions. Prices, promotions, and differentiated rules work without manual intervention while respecting existing ERP logic.
